change.description: perf(server): a checkpoint capture starts 8 git processes instead of 10 (#21315)
change.author: Joseph Vidal

contracts.action: Checkpoint capture resolves git common dir, user index path and HEAD existence with one combined `git rev-parse` instead of up to three separate processes
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code: resolveGitCommonDir (GitVcsDriver.ts:819), hasHeadCommit (GitVcsDriver.ts:793) and an inline `rev-parse --git-path index` inside the reused-index block. Those helpers are still used as the fallback.
contracts.before_after: Before: three separate rev-parse calls, with hasHeadCommit run inside the cleanup-guarded block. After: one call before the temp index is created. Exit 0 or 1 selects headExists, and a strict line count (4 or 3 lines plus a trailing empty line) gates the fast path. Any other shape (a newline in a path, git before 2.31 echoing --path-format) or an exit code other than 0 or 1 falls back to the old separate commands. The fallback keeps the old failure operation label (`GitVcsDriver.checkpoints.resolveGitCommonDir`). Nothing is created before the call, so cleanup ordering is unaffected.
contracts.visible_effect: Fewer git subprocesses per checkpoint capture (2 fewer with a committed HEAD, 1 fewer when HEAD is unborn). Checkpoint contents are unchanged. No UI change.
contracts.failure_mode: Outside a repository git exits 128, so the code takes the fallback and resolveGitCommonDir fails with the same error as before (covered by the new test). Unborn HEAD with --quiet exits 1 after printing the paths, which is handled. A path containing a newline raises the line count and uses the fallback (covered by the new test). A non-standard exit code with a valid line count is not trusted, because headChecked is false and hasHeadCommit is rerun.

summary: I found nothing to flag in this change. `resolveCaptureRepository` replaces up to three `git rev-parse` calls with one. It reads the exit code (0 for a committed HEAD, 1 for an unborn one) and checks the output line count before trusting it. Any other output shape, such as git before 2.31 or a path containing a newline, falls back to the old separate commands. The failure operation label for a non-repository is preserved. The new tests cover committed and unborn HEAD, a non-repository, and a newline in the path. The PR title says 8 processes instead of 10; by my count the saving is 2 for a committed HEAD and 1 for an unborn one, which I did not treat as a defect.
